title: US B-2 tourist visa
visa_description: For tourism, visiting family or friends, or medical treatment. A consular interview is part of the process.
source: Form DS-160, Online Nonimmigrant Visa Application (US Department of State)

questions.prompt: What's the main purpose of your trip to the United States?
Is the trip only for business meetings or a conference, with no tourism?
questions.help: A B-1/B-2 visa covers both, but Ta'asheera prepares the tourist (B-2) side for now.

stop_if.message: A business-only trip needs a B-1 visa, which Ta'asheera can't prepare yet. If you'll also travel for tourism, answer no.

questions.prompt: Will you work or take a course for credit in the United States?

stop_if.message: Work and study need a different US visa (such as H, F or J), which Ta'asheera can't prepare yet.

questions.prompt: Let's add your passport. You can upload a photo of its details page and confirm what we read, or type the details yourself.
When was your passport issued?

rules.message: The issue date can't be in the future.

questions.prompt: Have you ever lost a passport or had one stolen?
Which city or town were you born in?
And which country is that in?
What's your marital status?
What's your home address?
What's your main phone number?
questions.help: Include the country code, for example +961 71 123 456.

questions.prompt: What's your primary occupation?
What's the name and address of your employer or business, and your job title?
Which school or university do you attend?
When do you plan to arrive in the United States?
questions.help: Interview wait times can be long, so an estimate is fine.

rules.message: Your arrival date needs to be in the future.

questions.prompt: And when do you plan to leave?

rules.message: You can't leave before you arrive.
A visitor is usually admitted for up to 6 months. A longer stay needs a different visa.
Your passport must be valid for your whole stay. Many nationalities need 6 more months beyond it.

questions.prompt: Where will you stay in the United States? Give the name and address.
Who's your contact in the United States? Give their name, relationship to you and phone number, or the hotel's.
Who's paying for the trip?
Who's paying, and how are they related to you?
Is anyone travelling with you?
Have you ever been to the United States?
Have you ever been issued a US visa?
Have you ever been refused a US visa or entry to the United States?
questions.help: Answer honestly: the consulate sees earlier refusals, and a false answer can make you permanently ineligible.

documents.label: Digital photo
documents.help: Square, at least 600 x 600 pixels, colour, plain white background, taken in the last six months, no glasses.

documents.label: Bank statements
documents.help: Recent statements showing you can pay for the trip. Bring them to the interview too.

documents.label: Letter from your employer
documents.help: Your role, salary and approved leave: it helps show you'll return home.

documents.label: Business registration
documents.help: Your business registration and recent tax returns.

documents.label: Proof of enrolment
documents.help: A letter from your school or university confirming you're enrolled.

documents.label: Letter from whoever is paying
documents.help: A signed letter saying they'll pay, with their recent bank statements.

documents.label: Travel plans
documents.help: Your planned itinerary or hotel bookings. Optional, but useful at the interview.

documents.label: Previous visas
documents.help: Copies of earlier US or other visas, if you have them.
